description:
Filed s395 by #314 family F-A2 (the attribute STRIP), as the "new axes are
filed, not fixed" half of the filler rule.  See docs/not-supported.md
"Attributes on a variable declaration".

PCL strips an attribute list off a `my`/`our`/`state` declaration and announces
the drop.  What perl actually does at that point is a compile-time protocol:

  * look up MODIFY_SCALAR_ATTRIBUTES / MODIFY_ARRAY_ATTRIBUTES /
    MODIFY_HASH_ATTRIBUTES in the DECLARING package -- or, for a typed lexical
    (`my Dog $spot : plugh`), in that class -- and call it as
    ($package, $ref_to_fresh_var, @attrs);
  * whatever the handler RETURNS is the list of attributes it did not
    understand, and each of those is a compile error:
       Invalid SCALAR attribute: Foo at FILE line N.
  * attributes::get($ref) reads back what FETCH_*_ATTRIBUTES reports;
    attributes::reftype is the other half of that module.
  * subs have the same protocol with MODIFY_CODE_ATTRIBUTES, plus the builtin
    CODE attributes (:lvalue, :method) which perl handles itself.

MEASURED COST of not having it (s395, in the tree with the strip):
  t/op/attrs.t   0 -> 28 ok / 61 not-ok   (was a whole TRANSPILE-FAIL file)
  t/uni/attrs.t  0 ->  8 ok / 26 not-ok
The 61+26 are exactly this task: rows asserting the compile error, and rows
reading attributes back (crash signature `undef-fn:attributes::pl-_guess_stash`).

LAYER (CLAUDE.md 9a): the DISPATCH is a language mechanism -- the declaration
site must emit the call -- so the emitter owns it, keyed on the mechanism and
never on an attribute name.  `attributes.pm` itself (get/reftype/import) is a
lib/ shim; perl ships it as a .pm over an XS core, and the shim is the right
home for everything except the compile-time call.

BAR: probe the four handler shapes against perl (scalar/array/hash, plus a
typed lexical routing to the class); the unconsumed-return compile error must
fire with perl's message text where cheap; re-run op/attrs.t + uni/attrs.t and
splice their snapshot rows; gate; corpus-diff; sweep (a lib/ change makes the
full sweep non-optional, s377 rule).  The not-supported entry is DELETED by
this task, not rephrased.
subject: attribute protocol (MODIFY_*_ATTRIBUTES + attributes::get) - op/attrs.t 61 rows, uni/attrs.t 26
